claim: Across the three reported FY2026 quarters, Services YoY growth was Q1 +13.9%, Q2 +16.3%, Q3 +12.1% -- non-monotonic but with Q3 as the trough -- while iPhone YoY growth was consistently higher at 21-23% in every quarter, meaning FY2026 topline growth is currently iPhone/Greater-China led, not Services-led.
stance_target: Services growth deceleration through FY2026 / required Services CAGR to hold growth flat as hardware matures

claim: Greater China net sales grew 37.9% YoY in Q1 FY2026 (holiday quarter, $25,526M vs $18,513M PY), the strongest of the three FY2026 quarters, reflecting a sharp reversal of the multi-year China weakness narrative.
stance_target: Greater China is a structurally declining region for Apple

claim: Products gross margin rose to 40.7% in Q1 FY2026 from 39.3% PY, driven by product mix but 'partially offset by tariff costs' -- an explicit tariff-cost drag distinct from the Q3 filing's memory-cost callout, indicating cost pressures evolved in composition across FY2026 quarters.
stance_target: Component/tariff cost pressure on gross margin
quoted_support: Products gross margin and gross margin percentage increased during the first quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter in 2025 primarily due to a different mix of products, partially offset by tariff costs.

claim: R&D expense grew 31.7% YoY to $10,887M in Q1 FY2026, attributed to 'increases in infrastructure-related costs, headcount-related expenses and engineering program costs,' while capex fell YoY to $2,373M from $2,940M -- the third consecutive FY2026 quarter of rising R&D opex alongside falling capex.
stance_target: Apple's AI posture is deliberate capital discipline, not a capex arms race
quoted_support: The growth in research and development ("R&D") expense during the first quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter in 2025 was primarily driven by increases in infrastructure-related costs, headcount-related expenses and engineering program costs.

claim: As of the Q1 FY2026 filing (~January 2026), Apple disclosed a March 2, 2026 deadline to file a petition for rehearing of the Ninth Circuit's Epic v. Apple order, the procedural step preceding the May 21, 2026 Supreme Court certiorari petition and the June 30, 2026 cert grant disclosed in the Q3 filing.
stance_target: Timeline reconstruction of Epic v. Apple's path to the U.S. Supreme Court
scope_conditions: Apple Q1 FY2026 10-Q legal proceedings section
quoted_support: The deadline for the Company to file a petition for rehearing is March 2, 2026.

claim: Apple repurchased $25.0 billion / 93 million shares of common stock in Q1 FY2026 alone, the first of three consecutive quarterly buyback tranches (Q1 $25.0B, Q2 $36.0B, Q3 $25.8B) totaling roughly $61.8-86.8B across FY2026's first nine months.
stance_target: Buybacks raise EPS with no revenue growth, by shrinking the denominator
quoted_support: the Company repurchased 93 million shares of its common stock for $25.0 billion.
